packages.title: Local GHG end-user allocation QA
facts: DESNZ local GHG statistics spatially disaggregate national inventory emissions for local authorities.
CO2, CH4 and N2O are represented on an end-user basis in the local methodology.
Energy-supply emissions can be distributed according to where energy is ultimately used.
End-user allocation differs from direct parcel measurement.
No parcel emission value is inferred.

packages.title: Local GHG 71 percent authorities decrease QA
facts: DESNZ reports emissions decreased from 2023 to 2024 in 71% of UK local authority areas.
The release identifies 255 of 361 local authority areas with a decrease.
The comparison is between annual local-authority estimates.
The result is consistent with the overall UK emissions decrease in 2024.
The statistic does not describe every parcel within those authorities.

packages.title: Local GHG allocation exclusions QA
facts: The local GHG dataset excludes aviation, shipping and military transport from local allocation where there is no obvious allocation basis.
Fluorinated gases are also excluded from local estimates because suitable local allocation data are unavailable.
These exclusions differ from the full UK territorial inventory scope.
Excluded national emissions must not be silently redistributed to local areas.
Parcel values are not inferred from excluded categories.

packages.title: Local GHG LULUCF emissions and removals QA
facts: The local GHG technical report includes land use, land-use change and forestry methodology.
LULUCF can contain both emissions and removals.
CO2, CH4 and N2O components can have different signs and drivers.
Agricultural non-CO2 emissions are accounted for separately from LULUCF where appropriate.
A local LULUCF estimate is not a measured parcel carbon stock.

packages.title: Local GHG waste-arising allocation QA
facts: The local statistical release distributes waste emissions based on where waste arises.
Waste-emissions allocation therefore differs from assigning emissions to the treatment-facility location alone.
Waste tonnage is an activity measure rather than CO2e by itself.
Methodological allocation should be preserved when comparing local sources.
No parcel-level waste emission is inferred.

packages.title: Local GHG nationally consistent evidence-base QA
facts: DESNZ describes the local GHG estimates as a nationally consistent subnational evidence base.
The series covers estimates from 2005 to 2024.
National datasets underpin the local estimates.
The statistics can support local trend monitoring and mitigation planning.
Additional local monitoring can still be required for specific interventions.

packages.title: NAEI source versus end-user emissions QA
facts: NAEI publishes greenhouse-gas inventory information with source-based and end-user presentations.
Source-based emissions attribute releases to the emitting source.
End-user presentations can reallocate energy-supply emissions to consuming sectors.
The two accounting presentations must not be mixed within one comparison.
Neither presentation creates measured parcel emissions automatically.

packages.title: NAEI 1990 to 2024 inventory vintage QA
facts: NAEI lists the 2026 UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory covering 1990 to 2024.
Inventory vintages can revise historical years when methods or source data improve.
A publication-year label differs from the latest inventory data year.
Historical comparisons should preserve the inventory vintage.
Future 2025 final inventory values are not inferred from the 1990-2024 inventory.

packages.title: NAEI air pollutant versus greenhouse gas boundary QA
facts: NAEI publishes separate greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant datasets.
Air pollutants and greenhouse gases can arise from overlapping activities but use different inventories and metrics.
Concentration measurements are distinct from emissions inventories.
Ammonia is an air pollutant rather than a greenhouse gas.
Cross-inventory values are not treated as interchangeable.

packages.title: Pollution Inventory whole-permit scope QA
facts: The Environment Agency Pollution Inventory collates annual mass releases from regulated industrial sites.
Reporting covers the whole authorisation, licence or permit.
The dataset includes releases to air and water and waste transfers.
A permitted site boundary is not necessarily a cadastral parcel boundary.
Facility releases are not automatically assigned to a parcel.

packages.title: Pollution Inventory fugitive and point releases QA
facts: Pollution Inventory reporting includes specific point releases such as chimneys.
It also includes non-point and fugitive emissions such as leaks.
A single facility total can therefore aggregate multiple release mechanisms.
Point-source coordinates alone do not necessarily represent the full reporting boundary.
No parcel total is inferred from a point coordinate.

packages.title: Pollution Inventory 2013 to 2024 data-vintage QA
facts: The current Environment Agency data page provides annual downloadable Pollution Inventory files through 2024.
The resource includes historical annual files going back to at least 2013 on the current page.
Annual datasets should retain their reporting year.
Revised historical files can coexist with newer annual files.
A facility record year must not be substituted with another year.

packages.title: UK PRTR air water soil media QA
facts: UK PRTR datasets report industrial pollutant releases to air, water and soil.
The receiving environmental medium is part of the record meaning.
Different media must not be aggregated without an explicit compatible method.
PRTR pollutants include substances beyond greenhouse gases.
A PRTR release is not automatically a parcel GHG value.

packages.title: UK PRTR off-site transfer QA
facts: UK PRTR includes off-site transfers for treatment or disposal.
A transfer quantity is distinct from an on-site environmental release.
Waste transfer and pollutant release fields have different semantics.
Destination activity must not be assigned to the originating parcel as direct emissions without evidence.
No parcel CO2e is inferred from an off-site transfer.

packages.title: UK PRTR reporting threshold QA
facts: PRTR reporting uses pollutant and activity thresholds.
Absence of a reported value can reflect threshold rules rather than zero emissions.
Thresholded inventories require explicit missing-versus-zero handling.
Facility reporting status is not equivalent to parcel environmental performance.
No zero value is fabricated for non-reported records.

packages.title: 2026 conversion factors activity-based QA
facts: DESNZ 2026 conversion factors support calculation of GHG emissions from UK activities.
Activity-based calculations require compatible activity data and factor units.
A factor alone is not an emissions measurement.
The factor vintage should match the intended reporting context.
No parcel emissions are calculated without parcel activity data.

packages.title: 2026 activity versus spend-based factors QA
facts: DESNZ distinguishes its activity-based conversion factors from Defra spend-based emissions multipliers.
Spend-based multipliers can support initial supply-chain assessment when detailed activity data are unavailable.
Users are expected to disclose the method used.
Activity-based and spend-based results are not interchangeable without qualification.
No parcel result is inferred from spending categories alone.

packages.title: 2026 conversion-factor annual-vintage QA
facts: The government conversion-factor publication is explicitly the 2026 edition.
Regular users are directed to review changes for consistent year-on-year reporting.
Factor changes can affect comparability between reporting years.
A 2026 factor must not be silently substituted into a different historical methodology.
Factor metadata is preserved in QA.

packages.title: UK ETS 983,000 additional 2026 allowances QA
facts: The revised 2026 UK ETS auction calendar increased auction volume by 983,000 allowances.
The revision accounts for inclusion of maritime emissions.
The additional volume begins to be distributed across remaining auctions from 12 August 2026.
Auction supply is a market quantity rather than verified emissions.
No parcel emissions are inferred from allowance volume.

packages.title: UK ETS nearly 53 million allowances across 25 auctions QA
facts: DESNZ states just under 53 million allowances are scheduled across 25 auctions in 2026.
The 2026 auction programme began on 14 January 2026.
Auctions continue on a fortnightly schedule.
Auctioned allowances are tradable compliance instruments.
Allowance counts are not direct emissions measurements.

packages.title: UK ETS secondary market versus emissions QA
facts: UK ETS participants can trade allowances on the secondary market.
Registry accounts support allowance holding and transfer.
Trading activity can occur independently of an operator's current emissions rate.
Market prices and volumes are not verified-emissions values.
No facility or parcel emissions are inferred from a trade.
